title: Hardy-Weinberg and sample size

blocks.what_we_do: Calculate a control-only exact mid-p Hardy-Weinberg test and apply an explicit sample-size-aware screening rule.
blocks.why: Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium (HWE) predicts genotype proportions a^2, 2a(1-a) and (1-a)^2 under random mating and other idealised assumptions. Here a is the frequency of one allele; it is not the HWE test p-value. A deficit of heterozygotes can indicate calling errors, related parents or a mixture of populations. We test autosomal controls so a genuine disease effect in cases is less likely to drive exclusion. Mid-p reduces the conservatism of a discrete exact test. Larger samples detect smaller departures, so a fixed cutoff is not portable to every cohort. Our prespecified course rule is 10^(-6 - 0.001 * max(0, n_control - 1000)), applied using the non-missing control count at each site. At this course size it is 0.000001; above the 1,000-control calibration it becomes more stringent. This is a transparent teaching policy, not a universal recommended threshold. Compare distributions and heterozygote excess/deficit before adopting it elsewhere.
blocks.you_need: State 4.3 and its PSAM phenotype; no association results are used to choose the cutoff.
blocks.command:
```{r s4-4}
psam <- guided_table(paste0(guided_path(cfg, "4.3"), ".psam"))
controls <- guided_list(psam$IID[psam$Disease == "1"], guided_path(cfg, "4.4", "controls.txt"), TRUE)
report <- guided_path(cfg, "4.4", "hardy")
run_plink(cfg, c("--pfile", guided_path(cfg, "4.3"), "--keep", controls, "--chr", "1-22", "--hardy", "midp", "--out", report))
hwe <- guided_table(paste0(report, ".hardy"))
n_control <- as.numeric(hwe$HOM_A1_CT) + as.numeric(hwe$HET_A1_CT) + as.numeric(hwe$TWO_AX_CT)
cutoff <- 10^(-6 - 0.001 * pmax(0, n_control - 1000))
p <- as.numeric(hwe$MIDP)
exclude <- guided_list(hwe$ID[!is.na(p) & p < cutoff], guided_path(cfg, "4.4", "exclude.txt"))
run_plink(cfg, c("--pfile", guided_path(cfg, "4.3"), "--exclude", exclude, "--make-pgen", "--out", guided_path(cfg, "4.4")))
retained <- guided_table(paste0(guided_path(cfg, "4.4"), ".pvar"))$ID
stopifnot(!any(c("rs4988235", "rs12913832", "rs1426654") %in% retained))
ops <- guided_replay_lists(cfg, "4.4", "4.3")
guided_register(cfg, "4.4", "4.3", 1844, 238852, operations = ops)
```

Plain PLINK 2 command (use `bin\plink2.exe` on Windows):

```sh
bin/plink2 --pfile results/guided/s4-3_state --keep results/guided/s4-4_controls.txt --chr 1-22 --hardy midp --out results/guided/s4-4_hardy --threads 2 --memory 2048
bin/plink2 --pfile results/guided/s4-3_state --exclude results/guided/s4-4_exclude.txt --make-pgen --out results/guided/s4-4_state --threads 2 --memory 2048
```

`--keep` restricts only the diagnostic call to controls; `--chr 1-22` excludes sex chromosomes from this HWE calculation. `--hardy midp` reports the exact mid-p statistic; R applies the displayed sample-size rule and `--exclude` filters the full case/control matrix. `--pfile` selects the native input; `--make-pgen` writes a new copy; `--out` names its files. The helper appends `--threads 2` and `--memory 2048` for threads and workspace MiB.
blocks.expected_result:
167 variants excluded, leaving 238,852. Strong planted errors are not the only failures: eight unplanted sites and seven altered duplicate copies also fail, while some mild errors survive. rs4988235, rs12913832 and rs1426654 leave here and cannot be used as surviving module 5 markers.

The tested PLINK version is defined in `config.R` and recorded in
`software_versions.txt`. Validation: executable chunks and instructor reference counts passed on Windows.
blocks.troubleshooting: Stop at the first error. Check the named input and the previous step. Keep the command and console logs; do not substitute files from a different dataset version. See [troubleshooting](../docs/troubleshooting.md).
blocks.what_this_check_can_reveal: Calling errors and population mixture. The unplanted failures demonstrate why HWE failure is not proof of technical error, and why association loci cannot be rescued after seeing their p-values.
blocks.quick_check:
Can a mixture of two groups, each in HWE but with different allele frequencies, show a heterozygote deficit when pooled?

<details><summary>Show the answer</summary>

Yes. Pooling can produce a deficit even without genotyping error.

</details>
